description: Running sandboxed Python and JavaScript computations directly in the reader's browser with WebAssembly—zero server load on Raspberry Pi or static hosting.
summary:
One of the defining innovations of modern technical blogging is allowing readers to tweak parameters, verify equations, and run algorithms directly on the page.
In this dispatch, we demonstrate how Smidr utilizes WebAssembly (Pyodide) to execute code exclusively in the reader’s local web browser.
💡 Server Security & Resilience Guarantee Because this static site is hosted on a Raspberry Pi (or GitHub Pages), zero code is ever transmitted to or executed on the server. All Python scripts run in an isolated client-side WebAssembly sandbox. Infinite loops or intensive computations only impact the reader’s local thread and cannot crash or breach the host server. Live Python Sandbox (Pyodide WASM) Try running or editing the neural forward-pass below. When you click Run (WASM), the browser lazily loads Pyodide WebAssembly and calculates the activation values on your device:
title: Interactive Client-Side Code Runners with WebAssembly

description: Formulating optimal control policies for multi-rotor aerial robotics using linear quadratic regulators and full state feedback.
summary:
Designing trajectory controllers for autonomous aerial robotics requires balancing agile maneuverability with dynamic stability. As established in foundational optimal estimation theory by Kalman [kalman1960] and classical feedback principles [astrom2010] , we formulate a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) for a 6-DOF multi-rotor system1.
Mathematical Formulation The linearized continuous-time error dynamics around the hover equilibrium point are expressed via state-space representation:
$$\dot{x}(t) = A x(t) + B u(t)$$
title: Autonomous Quadrotor Trajectory Optimization with LQR
